https://www.thetimes.com/world/russia-uk.text: As 2022 winds up, we look back on 12 tumultuous months during which the curtain fell on the Elizabethan era and war returned to Europe. In June the nation partied for the Queen’s Platinum Jubilee — then queued to say goodbye three months later. God Save the King echoed around the tainted stadiums of Qatar as England fans embraced a strange new reality. In Ukraine, the crimes of Russia’s invasion became brutally apparent. At home, three prime ministers tried to calm the storm as energy prices and inflation soared. One was outlasted by a lettuce. All the while the celebrity bandwagon rolled on, with an Oscar slap, a WAG libel trial and a disgraced MP seeking absolution by eating bugs in the jungle.

image.caption: A burqa-clad woman braves the harsh Kabul winter to sit with her child and beg for food on January 6. Afghanistan’s economy collapsed after the Taliban seized power in August 2021

Novak Djokovic is held at Tullamarine airport, Melbourne, on January 5 over his refusal to take the Covid vaccine. He was deported 11 days later. His three-year ban from Australia was overturned last month
A tearful Adele posts a video on Instagram on January 20 to apologise for postponing her Las Vegas residency due to Covid and delivery delays. Her first show eventually took place on November 18
Attempting to prevent the invasion of Ukraine, France’s President Macron held socially distanced talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow, February 7
Desperate civilians gather at Lviv’s central train station hoping to flee to Poland following the Russian advance, February 27
Amid global unease, an ominous satellite image shows a three-mile Russian military convoy just 40 miles from Kyiv, heading towards the city
Preparing to engage with overwhelming Russian firepower, servicemen of the Ukrainian National Guard take positions in central Kyiv

On March 5 refugees on the outskirts of Kyiv huddle under a destroyed bridge as they wait to cross the Irpin River. Russia is accused of deliberately targeting evacuation corridors and killing civilians as they try to escape
The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge prompt accusations of cultural insensitivity on March 22 when they shake hands with local children through a fence on a trip to Jamaica

The Mossbourne Federation rowing team trains hard before breakfast on March 25 at the Royal Docks next to London City Airport. The team of secondary-school pupils from a deprived area of east London had recently beaten teams from Eton and other independent schools
Lia Thomas wins a trophy at the NCAA championships in Atlanta on March 17. The transgender swimmer’s victory intensified the debate around fairness in women’s sport

The aid worker Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe is reunited with her husband, Richard, and seven-year-old daughter, Gabriella, on British soil on March 17. She was detained for six years in Iran after being arrested on spying charges
Will Smith strikes Chris Rock on stage during the Oscars ceremony on March 28. Rock, who was hosting the event, offended the actor by making a joke about his wife’s shaved head

Yelena Burainchenko becomes the face of the human suffering in Kharkiv in Ukraine when her apartment building is shelled in early March. Her wounds are painted with green disinfectant in this picture, taken by Jack Hill and first published in The Times
During an unannounced visit to Kyiv on April 9 the prime minister, Boris Johnson, surveys the destruction with Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelensky
The bodies of civilians are strewn on Yablunska Street in Bucha, northwest of Kyiv, on April 2 after Russian forces withdrew from the city. It was the first alleged evidence of Russian war crimes
The day after losing the Champions League final to Real Madrid, the red half of Merseyside is still able to celebrate their team’s FA and Carabao cup wins
Liverpool fans on their way to the Champions League final at the Stade de France in Paris are tear-gassed by police who lost control of the crowd, May 28

Amber Heard and Johnny Depp air their dirty laundry in a Virginia court in May. Depp had sued his ex-wife for libel, going on to win $10 million; Heard countersued and won $2 million in compensatory damages at the same hearing

A courtroom sketch of Coleen Rooney and her husband, Wayne, during the ‘Wagatha Christie’ trial. Coleen was sued unsuccessfully for libel by Rebekah Vardy after naming her as the source of leaked stories to The Sun

The reality star Kim Kardashian appeared on the Met Gala red carpet on May 3 wearing Marilyn Monroe’s iconic ‘Happy birthday, Mr President’ dress. The late actress famously wore it to serenade President Kennedy in 1962
Flanked by the Duke of Cambridge, the imperial state crown and the Duchess of Cornwall, Prince Charles takes his mother’s place at the state opening of parliament, May 10
The jailed Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny appears by video link to a Moscow court as his appeal against a nine-year sentence is rejected
The Ukrainian folk-rap group Kalush Orchestra celebrate after their song Stefania wins the Eurovision Song Contest in Turin, May 14
Activists in Atlanta protest on May 14 against a potential Supreme Court ruling that could limit abortion rights in the US. This came to pass when Roe v Wade was reversed in June
Israeli police beat mourners at the funeral of Shireen Abu Akleh, a Palestinian Al Jazeera journalist, in Jerusalem, May 13. The Israeli army said it may have shot her by accident in the West Bank
The US artistic swimmer Anita Alvarez is rescued by her coach after falling unconscious performing at the World Aquatics Championships in Budapest, June 22
Prince William poses with a tourist, Laura Zuikauskas, after she and her husband, Vitalijus, spotted the future king selling copies of the Big Issue in London on June 9
Reunited at last — virtually — at Glastonbury. Paul McCartney sang I’ve Got a Feeling with the isolated vocals of John Lennon, his late collaborator, on the Pyramid Stage on June 25
No hard stares as Paddington Bear visits the Queen for tea at Buckingham Palace. The film was shown on June 4 to mark the monarch’s Platinum Jubilee
Passengers face long queuesas they check in at Manchester airport on June 13. Travel chaos was caused all over the country by staff shortages
England’s Chloe Kelly whips off her shirt in celebration after scoring the winner against Germany in the Euro 2022 final at Wembley on July 31

A giant mechanical bull is the star of the Commonwealth Games opening ceremony on July 28 in Birmingham. The sculpture, a nod to the city’s historic Bull Ring market, will stay on show after a campaign to stop it being dismantled
The Chinese driver Zhou Guanyu is lucky to survive a 160mph crash in his Alfa Romeo on the opening lap of the British Grand Prix at Silverstone, July 3

The farrier Garry Harland burns a heated metal shoe onto a hoof belonging to Connie, a 12-year-old thoroughbred mare, at his forge in Spofforth, North Yorkshire, July 25. The practice of “hot shoeing” ensures a perfect fit and, done correctly, causes the animal no pain
Residents in Leeds take a refreshing dip in a paddling pool after the Met Office issues its first red warning for extreme heat, July 19
Protesters in Sri Lanka demanding the resignation of President Gotabaya Rajapaksa invade the pool at his palace in Colombo, July 9
Japan’s former prime minister Shinzo Abe lies fatally wounded on July 8 after being shot at a rally in the western city of Nara
Attempting to flee the scene, Tetsuya Yamagami, Abe’s suspected attacker, is taken to the ground by security police

A lone sunbather soaks up the rays in a parched Hyde Park on August 11. Parts of England and Wales faced drought conditions and hosepipe bans after record high temperatures and very little rainfall over the summer
A residential area in Balochistan province, Pakistan, disappears under water on August 30. The countrywide floods killed more than 1,500 people
Archie Battersbee, 12, lies in hospital, severely brain-damaged. His parents lost a legal battle to keep him on life support and he died on August 6
A man is led away from Salman Rushdie after stabbing him before a lecture in upstate New York on August 12. The author lost the sight in one eye
Shia Muslim men in Afghanistan beat themselves with knives attached to chains as part of a procession to mark the martyrdom of Hussein on August 5
The FBI raid the former president Donald Trump’s Florida home on August 10. His handling of White House paperwork is under investigation
Critics of Sanna Marin, the Finnish prime minister, accused her of being unfit to lead when footage of her partying was leaked on August 17
Tensions simmer at the World Gravy Wrestling Championships in Rossendale, Lancashire, August 29
Downing Street waves goodbye to the outgoing PM, Boris Johnson, who seems in a greater rush to depart than his wife, Carrie, on September 6
On the same day the Queen meets Johnson’s replacement, Liz Truss, at Balmoral. It was to be the monarch’s final royal engagement

Queen Elizabeth II’s coffin arrives at Windsor Castle on September 19, with her beloved fell pony Emma also paying her respects. After a committal service at St George’s Chapel, the coffin was lowered into the Royal Vault. Her reign of 70 years and 214 days is the longest of any British monarch
The Queen’s coffin, borne on the state gun carriage of the Royal Navy and adorned with the imperial state crown, orb and sceptre, travels along the Mall on September 19
During the Queen’s funeral on September 19, a lone Coldstream Guardsman walks past a sea of flowers in Windsor
Members of the public file past King Charles III, the Princess Royal, the Earl of Wessex and the Duke of York as they stand vigil by their mother’s coffin at St Giles’ Cathedral in Edinburgh
This Morning’s Phillip Schofield and Holly Willoughby were accused of skipping the queue to see the Queen’s coffin. The pair insisted they had respected the rules set for the media
The TikTok viral sensations Hisao Mitani, 68, and his pet African spurred tortoise, Bon-chan, 25, take a very slow stroll through Tokyo on September 16
Nasibe Samsaei cuts off her ponytail outside the Iranian consulate in Istanbul. Protests erupted in Iran after the death in custody of Mahsa Amini, 22, on September 16
The great tennis rivals Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal well up after playing doubles in Federer’s last match before retirement, at the O2 on September 23
A dress is spray-painted on the model Bella Hadid during Paris Fashion Week by Dr Manel Torres, inventor of the liquid fibre Fabrican

The chancellor, Kwasi Kwarteng, tells the Conservative Party conference on October 3 that he is ‘Getting Britain moving’ — having crashed the pound days earlier with his mini-budget. He was sacked by Liz Truss the following week

With Truss’s reign wilting fast on October 14 after only a month as PM, the Daily Star sets up a live feed to an unrefrigerated lettuce to see if it would outlast her. Truss resigned 11 days later, handing victory to the leafy vegetable

The UK’s third prime minister of 2022, Rishi Sunak, delivers his first address to the nation from the steps of No 10 on October 25. He paid tribute to his predecessor, Truss, but admitted that ‘some mistakes were made’
The James Webb telescope’s image Pillars of Creation captures vast columns of dust and gas in the Eagle Nebula, 6,500- 7,000 light years from Earth
Smoke billows from the Kerch bridge, a vital link between Crimea and Russia, after a powerful truck bomb exploded on October 8
China’s leader, Xi Jinping, right, looks on as Hu Jintao, a former president, is forcibly ejected from the Party Congress in Beijing
Climate protesters throw tins of tomato soup at Vincent van Gogh’s painting Sunflowers before glueing themselves to the wall at the National Gallery in London, October 14
Emergency workers and members of the public in Seoul give first aid to victims after more than 150 people were killed in a crowd surge at a packed Halloween event
The supermodel Heidi Klum gives herself little wriggle room dressed as a worm at her annual Halloween party, held at the Sake No Hana restaurant in New York
As controversy swirls around his takeover of Twitter, Elon Musk posts a video of himself carrying a hand basin and declares: ‘Entering Twitter HQ — let that sink in!’
A Banksy artwork in the Ukrainian town of Borodyanka — one of seven to appear in the country in November — takes aim at Vladimir Putin’s love of judo
Three men are found by coastguards after stowing away on the rudder of a tanker on its 11-day journey from Nigeria to the Canary Islands, November 29
A warm embrace between Emmanuel Macron and Rishi Sunak at the Cop 27 climate summit in Egypt is hailed as a sign that the post-Brexit froideur in Anglo-French relations may be thawing
The North Korean leader, Kim Jong-un, watches a test flight of the Hwasong-17 ‘monster missile’ with his daughter, believed to be named Ju Ae, fuelling speculation she is next in line

Matt Hancock’s wandering hands evoke a sense of déjà vu as he kisses his partner, Gina Coladangelo, on November 27 after three weeks in the jungle. The MP finished third on I’m a Celebrity … Get Me Out of Here!

As the global population exceeds eight billion, a newborn is chosen to symbolise the milestone. Damian was granted the honour as the first baby to be registered in the Dominican Republic on November 15
Anti-lockdown protests spread across China at the end of the month as police and demonstrators clashed. Dissenters waved blank pieces of paper as a symbol of censorship
Ron DeSantis burnished his credentials to be the Republicans’ next presidential candidate — rather than Donald Trump — after being re-elected as governor of Florida at the US midterms
England’s Jordan Henderson and Jude Bellingham butt heads to celebrate Henderson’s opening goal in the 3-0 victory over Senegal at the World Cup in Qatar on December 4
Netflix releases a trailer of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex’s documentary series, Harry & Meghan, on December 1 — in the middle of a royal visit to America by the Prince and Princess of Wales

A moment of contemplation for the England captain, Harry Kane, after his team’s 2-1 quarter-final defeat against France in the World Cup, December 10. Despite scoring from the spot earlier, Kane’s 84th-minute penalty miss against the reigning champions once again shattered the nation’s dreams of footballing glory. Is it ever coming home?

Warnings are issued to locals after a huge walrus nicknamed Thor finds a convenient overnight rest stop at Calshot Beach in Hampshire, December 12. The jaded blubbery seafarer was first sighted in the Netherlands in early November and had been heading down the French coast

Boris Johnson makes a questionable sartorial statement during a downpour in Venice on December 11. The former prime minister and his wife, Carrie, were visiting the city to attend the wedding of the Tory “power couple” Sophia True and Declan Lyons

A triumphant Lionel Messi hoists the World Cup aloft after Argentina beat France on penalties at the Lusail Stadium in Qatar, December 18. The final, hailed as one of the most exciting in the tournament’s history, had finished 3-3 after extra time
The Elizabeth Tower in Westminster is framed by trees covered in a festive frosting of snow — as a severe cold snap combined with rail strikes spark the customary Christmas travel chaos, December 12
A fatally injured pregnant woman is taken from a maternity hospital damaged by Russian shelling in Mariupol, March 9

https://www.thetimes.com/article/police-.title: Police in race row after defaming black Royal Marine
https://www.thetimes.com/article/police-.text:
Police in West Yorkshire have been accused of racism after a high court judge found the force defamed a black Royal Marine in an email to his superiors.
It is the first time a force has been found to have committed the highest level of defamation, referred to as a Chase Level One libel.
The West Yorkshire force is facing substantial costs and damages.
In an email sent to a Royal Navy commander, the force accused the marine of “threats and blatant lies” stating his behaviour was “far below the standard expected of a member of the armed forces”.
The force sent the email before it had approached the marine with any allegations about his conduct or formally interviewed a complainant.
Mr Justice Johnson has concluded that the force’s chief constable did libel the man, who cannot be named for legal reasons.
A further hearing will determine costs and damages.
The marine told The Times that he believed the force’s conduct had been motivated by racism. “West Yorkshire Police sent that email not believing they were dealing with an actual Royal Marine,” he said. “They thought this was some fantasist black man harassing his white partner and they treated me with complete disdain.”
The police, who arrested the man the day after emailing his superiors in August 2020, took 14 months to submit a file to the Crown Prosecution Service, who dropped the case for lack of evidence.
Yair Cohen, of Cohen Davis Solicitors, who represented the marine, said: “There is a presumption that the police should be believed and this represented a breach of that trust.
“They simply made up their minds that this man was guilty and tried to ruin his life, saying he was not fit to be a soldier or member of the armed forces.”
The case came about because of a hearing in the family court concerning the marine’s access to his daughter after he split from the girl’s mother.
The mother broke a court order by taking the girl to Switzerland in the summer of 2020, prompting the marine to apply to the court for her return.
She contacted PC Cathryn Harrison alleging that an email sent to her by her former partner showed “harassment” and “controlling and coercive behaviour” and casting doubt on whether he really had joined the marines.
Harrison emailed his warrant officer. In it she said the couple were in a “messy custody battle” and alleged that the soldier used his military background as a means to control her.
The email added that the police would be seeking a charge of controlling and coercive behaviour/harassment and asked the Royal Navy to launch an internal investigation.
Johnson said the email “does not merely repeat but in effect endorses the allegations made by the claimant’s former partner”.
West Yorkshire Police said it was unable to comment because of legal proceedings.

image.caption: A high court judge found the force defamed a black Royal Marine
